processing: A semi-oxidised high-mountain oolong: picked, withered, cooled, tossed, then fixed by pan heat, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: Not well recorded; high-mountain oolongs are usually valued most in spring and autumn.
appearance_dry: Typical of high-mountain oolong: tight, dark green rolled leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of light high-mountain oolong: clear golden yellow.
appearance_wet: Whole leaves opening fully, with reddish edges.
taste_profile: No independent tasting record is widely available; lightly oxidised high-mountain oolongs in general are floral and smooth with a clean sweetness.

brewing.notes: Treat it like other rolled high-mountain oolong: a longer first steep to open the leaf, then shorter ones.

vintage_note: Nothing tea-specific is recorded about its sale. Usual for light high-mountain oolong is the current year's harvest, drunk fresh and stored sealed, with the season stated on the pack.
description:
Tengchong Oolong is a registered geographical indication mark from Tengchong in western Yunnan, on the western side of the southern Gaoligong range. Yunnan is pu-erh country, so an oolong from here is something of a curiosity.

The best-known growing area is around Xinghua village in Mazhan township, near the volcanic park, where a high-mountain oolong tea scenic area has been set up. A local company promotes the tea under the Jibian name, with products such as Qingxin, Xueyu and Jin Oolong. Its own materials give about 2,500 m for a garden at Qingjing Mountain and about 2,100 m for Wuhe township.

The process follows the familiar high-mountain oolong steps of withering, cooling, tossing and fixing. Little independent description of the cup exists, so expect what is typical of light high-mountain oolong: floral, smooth and clean, and judge it for yourself.

Brew it as you would a rolled oolong, with hot water and a slightly longer first steep. Ask whether the lot is the geographical indication product or simply tea from the area.
history: Little is documented about when oolong growing started in Tengchong or who introduced it. The clearest markers are recent: the geographical indication mark, and the Mazhan oolong scenic area, rated a national AAA site in 2015.
